text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Netanyahu adviser Bar-Illan: we may be able to accept a limited Palestinian state.
- Foreign Minister Levy gets frosty reception in Jordan.
- Major General Levine unhurt, Brigadier General Amitai slightly injured in attack on South Lebanon Army post.
- Coalition close to compromise on budget.
- Palestinian Authority cellular phone tender deadline extended.
- Hotels expect tourism slump to persist.
HAARETZ
- Arafat personally ordered capture of perpetrators of Beit-El attack from his Gaza office.
- U.S. Special Envoy Ross to Middle East today to advance Hebron talks.
- German Foreign Minister Kinkel to Haaretz: Germany may need to re-evaluate ties with Iran.
- Likud, Fatah youth negotiate in Oslo.
- Deputy director of Prime Minister's Office: Bezek, Israel Chemicals, large part of banks, real estate companies to be privatised in 1997.
- 8 percent drop in Tel Aviv large apartment prices in Q3.
GLOBES
- Banker Edmond Safra reassesses possibility to buy Bank Leumi, asks treasury to open new tender.
- Heineken conditions entrance to Tempo on forcing Bar or Podhortzer from company.
- 23 percent drop in tourist nights in november; 39 percent rise in Israeli hotel stays.
MAARIV
- Ross to try to finish Hebron deal within a week.
- President Weizman informs Netanyahu: I'll run for second term.
- Army preparing for explosion with Palestinian police.
- Poll: Netanyahu rated lowest of all senior ministers.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Ross arrives tomorrow to finish negotiations on Hebron; peace teams finished drafting redeployment deal; Arafat, Netanyahu said to meet this week to solve last disputes.
- U.S. Ambassador Indyk: Palestinians must make concessions, Arafat ready to finish negotiations.
- Poll: 68% not satisfied with Netanyahu decision making.
- Settler council to Netanyahu: settlements or a battle against you.
